newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Stockbroker in Malaysia's biggest bank takeover.
newsitem.headline: Stockbroker in Malaysia's biggest bank takeover.

text.p: Malaysia's largest stockbroker, Rashid Hussain Bhd, announced on Tuesday the biggest bank merger in the nation's history.

It finalised a deal to acquire 75 percent of equity in Kwong Yik Bank Bhd from Malaysia's largest commercial bank, Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank), at 8.80 ringgit ($3.50) per share. Talks on the price took nearly a month.

Rashid also announced a series of related deals in which Kwong Yik will merge with its 20 percent owned associate DCB Holdings Bhd's banking unit, DCB Bank Bhd, and Kwong Yik Finance Bhd will merge with DCB Finance Bhd.
Analysts hailed the deal, saying the inclusion of Kwong Yik would improve the quality of Rashid Hussain's earnings.
Maybank is also expected to benefit, as it will have a substantial hoard of cash to expand its operations including making regional acquisitions.

"The deal is very positive for Rashid Hussain. Before, its earnings came predominantly from stockbroking, but this can be quite volatile. Now its earnings should be more stable and, there should be more earnings," said Lorraine Tan, an analyst at HLG Securities.

Rashid Hussain itself would not close the door to further bank mergers. Executive chairman Abdul Rashid, in answer to a reporter's question on Tuesday, said the firm was interested in regional expansions where it saw opportunities.

To finance the 2.16 billion ringgit ($857 million) buy, Rashid will sell shares amounting to 10 percent of its equity to construction and property firm Malaysian Resources Corp Bhd and also issue bonds to raise 800 million ringgit.

The entire deal will increase Rashid's stake in DCB Holdings to 54.17 percent from around 20 now, without disturbing Abdul Rashid Hussain's control over the stockbroking company. He and his family will hold a 30 percent stake in Rashid.
"DCB Bank and Kwong Yik Bank is a perfect fit," Abdul Rashid told a news conference to announce the deal.
"I see enormous potential for the merged bank to produce long-term earnings growth," he said. He announced the entire deal would be completed in six months.
Executives at Rashid said the merger was in response to the central bank Bank Negara's urgings for the industry to consolidate through mergers as the economy opens up to international competition.
They said the merged bank will become the country's second largest in terms of profit and the third largest in assets. The merged bank will have assets totalling 32 billion ringgit.
The new bank will have little overlap, Abdul Rashid said, adding that he had looked at other banks for merger candidates but found Kwong Yik to be the most suitable.
